storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands on the mobility and ubiquity of the broadcast apparatus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the active militarization of public acoustic space.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the content and duration of the ideological barrage.

storyboard.claim: Counterpoint means voices are entirely equal — something authoritarianism cannot tolerate.

left.label: COUNTERPOINT
left.subject: Two musicians, a young Chinese violinist and pianist, engaged in an equal, expressive musical duet in a classical practice room.

storyboard.claim: Totalitarianism demands unison: one single leader melody that everyone must mimic.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly contrasts the musical ideal with political regimentation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes visual the difference between harmony of equals and forced conformity.

storyboard.claim: Everyone must either sing the party's exact melody or act as subservient accompaniment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ranks of uniformed students singing revolutionary songs in robotic unison.
storyboard.onScreenText: EVERYONE MUST SING THE EXACT SAME MELODY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrates the practical enforcement of unison in cultural life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the erasure of individual voice in mass rallies.

storyboard.onScreenText: FORMALIST CAPITALIST POISON — VALUE OUTSIDE THE COLLECTIVE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Articulates the Red Guard ideology that criminalized polyphony.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the trauma to Sparrow himself, the master of counterpoint.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Translates the auditory shouting into the physical environment of written accusations.
